Job Title
: Founding Executive Director, Center for Translational Research in Behavioral Science
Department:

Assistant Provost for Research, Assessment, and Institutional Effectiveness
Location:

About Palo Alto University (PAU)

Palo Alto University is a private, nonprofit university dedicated to advancing human understanding through innovative education, groundbreaking research, and impactful practice in behavioral science.
Founded in 1975 and located in the heart of Silicon Valley, PAU offers graduate and undergraduate programs in psychology, counseling, social work, and behavioral science, including the PAU-Stanford PsyD Consortium with Stanford Medicine. Grounded in human dignity, PAU’s scholars, clinicians, educators, and learners share a single conviction: that understanding how people think, feel, behave, relate, heal, and make meaning is among the most essential work of our time.
The university enrolls over 1,200 students, has a network of more than 4,200 alumni, and employs over 150 faculty and staff who are united by a mission-driven commitment to advancing human understanding. PAU enters its sixth decade at a defining moment: a new president, a new provost, a bold new vision and strategic plan, and an urgent opportunity to shape how behavioral science responds to the challenges of an increasingly changing world. You will join a mission-driven community with the ambition to make a measurable impact on the human condition.

About the Position

The Founding Executive Director of the Center for Translational Research in Behavioral Science will establish and lead a university-wide hub that expands PAU’s research capacity, advances faculty and student research development, increases external funding, fosters interdisciplinary and strategic partnerships, and accelerates the translation of behavioral science research into meaningful real-world impact.
The successful candidate will be an entrepreneurial and collaborative leader who can build the Center from the ground up while developing innovative approaches to strengthen PAU’s research culture, visibility, partnerships, and impact.

SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Center for Translational Research
Establish and lead the Center, including its strategy, programs, operations, budget, partnerships, and measures of success.
Supervise research-related functions including the library, IRB, grants, writing support, and research design and data analysis services.
Develop signature research initiatives that translate PAU scholarship into meaningful applications in practice, policy, technology, and communities.
Engage faculty across the University as Center affiliates, collaborators, and research leaders.
Build strategic partnerships with universities, healthcare organizations, community organizations, government, foundations, and industry.
Support Presidential initiatives and University advancement priorities by identifying and developing research opportunities, partnerships, and external engagement aligned with PAU’s strategic goals.

Research Innovation & Strategy
Actively build and expand PAU’s research enterprise and generate meaningful external revenue through grants, sponsored research, contracts, and strategic partnerships.
Establish and achieve measurable research growth and revenue targets aligned with PAU’s Strategic Plan, while ensuring that all activities advance the University’s academic mission, research priorities, and long-term sustainability.
Identify opportunities to strengthen research infrastructure, productivity, interdisciplinary collaboration, visibility, and impact.
Advance translational research aligned with PAU’s strengths in psychology, counseling, and social work.
Advance PAU’s signature research agenda at the intersection of human understanding and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, positioning the University as a distinctive and influential voice in one of the most consequential areas of inquiry and innovation of our time.
Oversee the full portfolio of technology transfer and commercialization activities, including technology and licensing agreements, intellectual property management, invention disclosures, technology partnerships, royalty arrangements, and equity interests.

Research Development & Support
Identify external funding opportunities and support faculty in developing competitive grant proposals.
Convene and support interdisciplinary teams pursuing collaborative and strategically important research opportunities.
Develop workshops, mentoring, seed funding, and other initiatives that strengthen faculty research capacity and student research competencies.
Collaborate with University offices responsible for finance, faculty success, advancement, and other areas supporting the research enterprise.

External Engagement & Impact
Represent PAU and the Center with research partners, funders, and professional organizations.
Develop opportunities for external research partnerships, sponsored research, and philanthropic support.
Increase the visibility of PAU research and communicate its scholarly and societal impact.
Leverage PAU’s Silicon Valley location to develop innovative partnerships at the intersection of behavioral science, mental health, technology, and human-centered innovation.
Develop and cultivate strategic relationships with startups, accelerators, and venture capital firms to build partnerships, advance commercialization opportunities, and generate sustainable long-term revenue streams.

ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS
PhD or equivalent terminal research doctorate in psychology, behavioral science, health science, social science, or another field related to PAU’s areas of expertise.
Minimum of 3–5 years of research administration, research development, sponsored research, or related experience in a university or research environment.
Progressive leadership experience with demonstrated success developing programs, initiatives, partnerships, or research infrastructure.
Demonstrated understanding of external research funding and the academic research enterprise.
Experience supporting competitive grant proposals and collaborative research initiatives.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively with students, faculty, academic leaders, and external partners.
Ability to work in person, with established professional networks and connections across the San Francisco Bay Area.
Excellent leadership, communication, organizational, and project-management skills.
Demonstrated ability to think strategically, build new initiatives, and work collaboratively across disciplines and organizational boundaries.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
Demonstrated success securing or contributing substantially to externally funded research.
Genuine interest in and intellectual curiosity about research at the intersection of human understanding, emerging technologies, and artificial intelligence.
Experience developing interdisciplinary, multi-investigator, or multi-institutional proposals.
Experience launching or leading a research center, institute, or major research initiative.
Experience with translational, applied, implementation, or community-engaged research.
Familiarity with federal funding agencies relevant to PAU, including NIH, NSF, HRSA, and SAMHSA.
Record of scholarly accomplishment and experience supporting faculty research development.
Experience developing partnerships across academia, healthcare, government, foundations, community organizations, or industry.

Work Hours and Location

This is a full-time, residential position based at PAU's campuses in Palo Alto and Mountain View, California. Regular in-person presence is expected and essential to the community-building culture the Director is responsible for creating and sustaining. Occasional evening and weekend availability is required for student programs, events, and community initiatives.

In compliance with all applicable federal and state laws, employment decisions will be made without regard to any status protected by applicable law. The University will provide reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities consistent with applicable law.

jobs.description:
The California State University Auxiliary for Sponsored Programs Administration (SPA) as a non-profit, financially self-sufficient auxiliary organization that supports the mission of California State University Bakersfield through a variety of operations and services, such as federal and non-federal research and sponsored projects and other services and activities.

CANDIDATES ELIGIBLE TO APPLY:
Open to all qualified applicants

CLASSIFICATION TITLE:
Project & Outreach Coordinator

TEMPORARY END DATE:
This position is temporary and ends on or before June 30, 2027. Any continuation beyond June 30, 2027, is contingent upon satisfactory performance and available funding.

FT/PT:
Full-time

WORKPLACE TYPE:
On-site (work in-person at business location)

ANTICIPATED HIRING RANGE
: Starting salary upon appointment is not expected to exceed $5,000 per month

BENEFITS:
CSUB Auxiliary for Sponsored Programs Administration (SPA) offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, vacation and sick leave accrual, and 15 paid holidays per year. For more details, please visit our Auxiliary website.

POSITION PURPOSE:
The MESA (Mathematics, Engineering, Science Achievement) Program supports educationally and economically disadvantaged students pursuing degrees in STEM disciplines by providing academic support, career development, transfer preparation, and leadership opportunities. The program promotes student success, persistence, graduation, and transfer to four-year institutions through comprehensive academic and professional development services.

Under the general supervision of the NSME GO Director, the MESA Program Director is responsible for the day-to-day administration, coordination, implementation, and evaluation of the MESA Program. The incumbent develops and manages student success initiatives, monitors expenditures and assists with budget planning, coordinates academic support services, recruits and advises students, leads tutors and student assistants, prepares required state reports, and collaborates with faculty, administrators, and industry partners to ensure compliance with grant requirements and successful achievement of program objectives.

Duties & Responsibilities

Program Administration & Grant Management

Coordinate daily operations of the MESA Program by maintaining program calendars, activity schedules, work plans, reporting deadlines, and records of required grant deliverables.
Ensure compliance with grant requirements by applying established requirements to program operations, maintaining supporting compliance documentation, and bringing unclear requirements, potential compliance issues, or requested exceptions to the Director for resolution.
Maintain student eligibility and program records by reviewing records for missing or inconsistent information, obtaining necessary documentation, and protecting confidential student information in accordance with applicable requirements.
Prepare required programmatic, fiscal, and assessment reports by compiling narrative and statistical information, verifying data, coordinating contributions from program personnel, incorporating requested revisions, and routing reports for review and approval.
Monitor expenditures and assist with budget planning by compiling prior-year expenditures, anticipated program costs, and projected activity needs. Initiate and track approved purchases and expenditures in accordance with university procedures.
Evaluate program effectiveness and recommend improvements by comparing program participation, service utilization, retention, and other established performance measures against grant objectives. Identify trends, unmet targets, and operational concerns and recommend adjustments to outreach, services, schedules, or procedures for the Director's consideration.

Student Success, Advising & Program Coordination

Recruit and admit eligible MESA students by explaining MESA eligibility requirements, services, participation expectations, and application procedures to prospective students. Review applications and supporting documentation, determine eligibility based on established criteria, and refer unusual circumstances or requested exceptions to the Director.
Coordinate academic advising, tutoring, career development, and transfer activities by developing schedules, reserving facilities, communicating with service providers and participants, tracking attendance, and resolving routine scheduling or participation issues.
Plan workshops, industry speakers, field trips, and professional development opportunities by coordinating presenters, facilities, registration, materials, transportation requirements, participant communications, and event evaluations.
Develop student retention initiatives based on program data, student feedback, and identified service needs. Implement approved activities, monitor participation, evaluate results against established objectives, and recommend modifications.

Collaboration, Outreach & Partnerships

Collaborate with faculty, counselors, administrators, and community partners that support MESA students and program objectives.
Promote MESA services across campus through presentations, campus events, informational materials, email communications, web content, and other approved outreach methods. Ensure that published information is accurate, current, and consistent with program requirements.
Develop partnerships with industry, universities, and STEM organizations.
Participate in collaborative grant development by compiling program data, describing existing services and outcomes, gathering partner information or letters of support, participating in planning meetings, and reviewing assigned proposal sections for accuracy.

Personnel Lead Direction and Program Support

Coordinate the recruitment and hiring process for tutors, peer mentors, and student assistants by publicizing openings, reviewing applications against established requirements, participating in interviews, providing recommendations, and completing required hiring documentation.
Orient and train student employees regarding assigned responsibilities, program procedures, service expectations, confidentiality requirements, recordkeeping, and appropriate referral of student concerns.
Develop work schedules, assign duties, communicate priorities and deadlines, and monitor staffing coverage for tutoring, outreach, workshops, and other program activities.
Review completed work, tutoring records, attendance documentation, and other assigned deliverables for accuracy and completeness. Provide routine feedback and guidance and refer significant performance or conduct concerns to the Director.
Coordinate tutoring and supplemental instruction services by matching available tutors with program needs, maintaining schedules and service records, monitoring participation, and addressing routine scheduling or service-delivery problems.

Required Qualifications

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE -
Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university, preferably in a mathematics-based, engineering, science, or related STEM discipline. Two years of progressively responsible professional experience working with postsecondary students. Experience coordinating educational or student support programs. Experience providing academic advising, student success services, or related programming. Experience managing projects, budgets, or grant-funded initiatives.

LICENSES: Possession of a valid driver's license or the ability to obtain by date of hire.

SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & ABILITIES (SKA's) -

Regular and reliable attendance is required.
Working knowledge of student development principles and student success programming.
Working knowledge of grant administration, compliance, and budget-monitoring practices.
Skill in independently planning, organizing, and coordinating multiple projects and competing priorities using sound judgment and project management practices.
Project management skills.
Skill in collecting, maintaining, analyzing, and reporting program data and evaluating program effectiveness.
Ability to establish collaborative relationships with faculty, administrators, community organizations, and industry partners.
Ability to train, schedule, and provide work direction and oversight to student employees and tutors.
Ability to work effectively with students from diverse backgrounds and recognize and respond to differing student needs.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, student information systems, and database management.
Demonstrated customer service experience requiring a very high level of diplomacy and professionalism.
Ability to use tact and diplomacy to effectively handle a broad range of high level and sensitive interpersonal situations with diverse personalities, and to respond appropriately to conflicts and problems.
Ability to initiate, establish, and foster communication and teamwork by maintaining a positive, cooperative, productive work atmosphere in the University with the ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships within a diverse population and with those from various cultural backgrounds.
Excellent communication skills; ability to effectively communicate information in a clear and understandable manner.
Thorough knowledge of English grammar, spelling, and punctuation.
Ability to interpret, communicate and apply policies and procedures.
Ability to maintain a high degree of confidentiality.
Excellent organizational and time management skills with the ability to set own priorities to coordinate multiple assignments with fluctuating and time-sensitive deadlines.
Excellent computer skills and competence with a variety of computer applications including word-processing, spreadsheets, databases, on-line systems, Internet as well as online calendaring and email.
Working knowledge of or ability to quickly learn University infrastructure.
Must be willing to travel and attend training programs off-site for occasional professional development.
Must be able to work occasional holidays and adjust working hours to meet special jobs. May be called back periodically to perform work as needed on an emergency basis.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in education, counseling, STEM, higher education administration, or a related field.
Experience administering state or federally funded grants.
Experience working in MESA, TRIO, EOP, STEM, or similar student success programs.
Familiarity with California Community College systems and transfer pathways.
Experience developing partnerships with industry and four-year universities.
Demonstrated skills in an institutional/educational environment possessing a customer-oriented and service-centered attitude.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:
SEDENTARY WORK
- involves mainly sitting; minimal walking and standing; lifting light weight objects limited to 15 pounds.

ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS:
N/A

Special Conditions

SCREENING:
Only those applicants possessing experience most directly related to the immediate needs of the office will be invited to appear before a Qualifications Appraisal Board for the purpose of appraising training, experience, and interest in the position .

BACKGROUND CHECK:
Satisfactory completion of a background check (including a criminal records check) is required for employment. CSU Bakersfield Auxiliary for Sponsored Programs Administration (SPA) will make a conditional offer of employment, which may be rescinded if the background check reveals disqualifying information, and/or it is discovered that the candidate knowingly withheld or falsified information. Failure to satisfactorily complete the background check may affect the continued employment of a current employee who was conditionally offered the position.

The mission of Social Capital Initiatives is to leverage the power of social capital to improve livelihoods in under-served communities by promoting education, healthcare, and sustainable development.

With a particular focus on women, girls, and their families, Social Capital Initiatives utilizes its proven Social Capital Credits (SoCCs) methodology—along with innovative programs and technologies—to empower people to realize their potential and become active stakeholders in their own success. Founded 26 years ago, Social Capital Initiatives now reaches more than 100,000 people every year across 25 communities in Asia, the U.S., Africa, and Europe.

To achieve this vision, Social Capital Initiatives is seeking a dynamic and visionary executive who can work with its Founder and the Board to scale the organization into its next stage of growth.

Fundraising expertise, with established connections in the philanthropic community and demonstrated success with major donors, corporations, foundations, and government agencies. Knowledge of the corporate donor ecosystem in India is an added plus.

Experience working effectively with a Board of Directors.

Entrepreneurial approach to growth, sustainability, and innovation—balancing mission focus with business discipline.

The executive director provides strategic leadership for a broad portfolio that includes Occupancy Management, Budget and Finance, Communications and Assessment, Technology and Housing Systems, and Living-Learning Programs. A central focus of the position will be developing and implementing strategies to strengthen demand for campus housing, optimize occupancy and revenue, enhance the residential student experience, and ensure that housing strategies align with the University's broader enrollment, academic, and student success priorities. The executive director will bring a data-informed, forward-thinking approach to these efforts, identifying opportunities to strengthen operations, improve effectiveness, and position HDP to respond successfully to evolving student needs and market conditions.

The executive director will join a highly collaborative leadership team committed to innovation, thoughtful decision-making, continuous improvement, and the long-term success of Housing & Dining Programs. The position offers the opportunity to work across institutional boundaries, build strong partnerships with key University stakeholders, and play an important role in advancing both the department's priorities and the University of Utah's broader strategic goals.

The executive director manages a dynamic team of 19 professionals, including four direct reports, and administers an annual budget of approximately $5 million.

Responsibilities

Occupancy, Enrollment, and Housing Strategy

Provide executive leadership for the U's housing occupancy strategy, including demand forecasting, application and contracting processes, room selection, assignments, and strategies designed to maximize utilization of the U's residential inventory.
Leverage enrollment, occupancy, market, and historical data to develop projections and identify opportunities to strengthen housing demand and achieve consistently high occupancy.
Partner closely with Enrollment Management, Admissions, academic colleges, Athletics, International Student Programs, and other institutional stakeholders to position housing as an important component of student recruitment, enrollment, retention, and success.

Business and Financial Leadership

Identify, research, and analyze strategic opportunities and evaluate their operational, fiscal, and policy implications in conjunction with centralized fiscal operations.
Provide recommendations to executive leadership that support sound decision-making and the long-term financial sustainability of Housing & Dining Programs.

Technology, Data, and Assessment

Maintain strategic oversight of housing technology and information systems, including the department's StarRez housing management platform, technology integrations, and systems supporting housing operations.
Champion a data-informed culture by ensuring that occupancy information, student feedback, assessment results, financial data, and institutional metrics translate into actionable strategies for continuous improvement.
Oversee the departmental assessment planning, data collection, analysis, reporting, and integration of findings into strategic and operational plans.

Communications, Marketing, and Outreach

Guide the strategic planning and implementation of departmental communications, marketing, outreach, and recruitment efforts.
Ensure that Housing & Dining Programs communicates effectively with prospective and current students, families, campus partners, and other stakeholders, and develops marketing and outreach strategies that support occupancy and enrollment objectives.

Living-Learning Programs

Set strategic priorities and provide executive oversight for the university's living-learning and themed residential communities.
Partner with academic colleges and other campus organizations to ensure residential programs support institutional priorities while creating meaningful opportunities for student engagement, belonging, and academic success.

Organizational Leadership

Recruit, develop, supervise, and evaluate professional staff while creating a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and professional growth.
Serve as a strategic advisor to the associate vice president and contribute broadly to the success of Housing & Dining Programs beyond the assigned portfolio.

The Director of Development leads IA&A's philanthropic strategy and is responsible for building the organization's contributed revenue base across foundations, government sources, corporate partners, and individual donors. IA&A has historically operated on a near-total reliance on earned revenue. The 2026-2030 strategic plan calls for a more diversified model in which contributed revenue becomes a meaningful and growing share of the organization's resource base. The Director of Development is the architect of that shift.

The work includes building IA&A's first sustained culture of philanthropy, developing a major gifts program, deepening foundation and government grant work, growing corporate partnerships tied to the organization's cultural diplomacy mission, and supporting the Board's expanded role in fundraising. The Director works in close partnership with the President & CEO, who personally cultivates and closes major funders, and collaborates with the COO, Vice President of Exhibitions and other senior staff to develop fundable programs and a compelling case for support.

Duties and responsibilities

Strategy & Planning

Develop and execute a multi-year contributed revenue plan aligned with the 2026-2030 strategic plan, with annual goals across foundation, government, corporate, individual, and planned giving sources.
Build IA&A's first sustained culture of philanthropy across staff, Board, and external supporters in an organization that has not historically relied on contributed income.
Partner with the CEO and senior program leadership to identify fundable programs and shape compelling cases for support, including for the integration of TES, Hillyer, and CEP as a unified cultural diplomacy platform.
Establish the policies, systems, and reporting needed to support a growing development operation, including within the Bloomerang and Monday CRM systems, gift acceptance, recognition, and donor stewardship practices.

Foundation & Government Funding

Cultivate and steward a portfolio of institutional funders, including private and family foundations, DCAH, the National Endowment for the Arts, the National Endowment for the Humanities, and other government cultural programs.
Oversee all grant writing and reporting, including direct authorship of major proposals and supervision of any external grant writers or consultants.
Build a balanced pipeline of project-restricted and general operating support.

Corporate & International Partnerships

Develop a corporate giving and sponsorship program connected to IA&A's cultural diplomacy mission, with particular attention to companies with international footprints and brands aligned with arts and culture.
Build sponsorship opportunities tied to specific exhibitions, programs, and events, including exhibition tours, Hillyer programming, and signature convenings.
In partnership with the CEO, identify and develop funding relationships with embassies, international foundations, and binational cultural organizations.

Individual Giving & Major Gifts

Build IA&A's individual donor base, including a focused major gifts program calibrated to the organization's size and growth stage.
Personally manage a portfolio of major donor prospects; staff the CEO and Board members on their portfolios with briefings, materials, and follow-through.
Develop annual giving, membership, and donor engagement structures sized to what is sustainable for an organization of IA&A's scale, and build a planned giving program over time.

Board Engagement

Support 100% Board giving and active Board engagement in fundraising; work with the CEO and Board leadership to formalize give/get expectations.
Staff the Development Committee (or any merged Development and Nominating committee structure) and serve as the senior staff resource for Board fundraising activity.
Equip Board members with the tools, briefings, and prospect support they need to participate appropriately in cultivation and solicitation.

Events, Communications & Donor Experience

Plan and execute fundraising and cultivation events, including donor receptions, exhibition openings, and signature annual events.
Use Hillyer and the IA&A programmatic calendar as a primary platform for donor cultivation and stewardship.
Work with the Communications staff to ensure development materials, donor communications, and the public case for support are consistent with the IA&A brand and strategic plan.

Team & Operations

Build and lead the development function, including any Development staff and management of external development consultants.
Maintain accurate donor records, gift processing, and reporting; provide regular forecasting to the CEO and Board.
Recruit and onboard additional development staff as the function grows and capacity is justified.
Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Seven or more years of progressive fundraising experience in the nonprofit sector; experience in arts, culture, museums, or international affairs preferred.
Demonstrated success building or substantially growing a development program, including direct authorship of grants and direct cultivation of major gifts.
Experience across foundation, government, corporate, and individual sources, with a track record of securing meaningful institutional and individual support.
Experience building a development function in a smaller or early-stage shop, including establishing systems, processes, and donor culture where they did not previously exist.
Strong written and oral communication skills; ability to translate organizational strategy into a compelling case for support.
Comfort working in close partnership with a CEO and Board, and supporting both in their respective fundraising roles.
Experience with CRM and donor database systems; Bloomerang and Monday.com, or similar preferred.
Familiarity with cultural diplomacy, international arts, or embassy and diplomatic networks is an asset but not required.
Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree or CFRE credential preferred.

Working conditions

International Arts & Artists is located in the historic Dupont Circle neighborhood of Washington, D.C. All IA&A staff work onsite and are expected to maintain regular work hours in alignment with the Employee Manual. The Director of Development will regularly be required to work outside of regular business hours, including evenings and weekends for events and exhibition openings. Travel is approximately 10-15%, primarily domestic, for donor meetings, foundation visits, and conferences. IA&A currently maintains an open workspace with low to moderate noise.

Physical requirements

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand, sit, talk, hear, and use hands and fingers to operate a computer and telephone keyboard. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision requirements due to computer work.

jobs.description:
Fractional Director of Development & New Partnerships

Cancer Pathways  |  Seattle, WA  |  Hybrid
Independent Contractor  |  Part-Time, Up to 20 Hours/Week
The Opportunity

Cancer Pathways has an opening for an experienced, relationship-driven fundraiser who can create new revenue opportunities quickly while building relationships that can grow into significant long-term support.  This is a results-oriented engagement. We are looking for someone who can quickly build a qualified new-business pipeline, create new donor and corporate relationships, and begin generating new revenue within the first few months.
We need someone who can come in, quickly understand our mission and story, identify where the strongest opportunities exist, and begin opening doors with new individual donors, corporate partners, sponsors and other prospective funders. This is not a role where success means developing a strategy that may eventually produce results — we need both strategy and execution, with urgency.
At the same time, we know meaningful philanthropy is built on relationships. We are not looking for someone who equates fundraising with sending large volumes of cold emails or making premature asks. We want someone who knows how to find the right prospects, create a path to them, build genuine relationships, recognize when an opportunity can move quickly, and thoughtfully cultivate those that require more time.
About Cancer Pathways

Cancer changes lives overnight. Cancer Pathways makes sure no one has to navigate it alone.
For 30 years, Cancer Pathways has provided free support, education and community for anyone impacted by cancer. Our programs include support groups, educational workshops, youth camps, prevention and education programs, and community events.
Nearly 500,000 people have been touched by our programs. As we look toward the future, we will be significantly expanding our reach and impact, which also means we need to expand the community of individuals and organizations investing in our mission.
Primary Responsibilities

Generate new philanthropic revenue for Cancer Pathways from individuals, corporations, sponsors and other sources.
Quickly identify the strongest near-term opportunities for new funding and actively pursue them, while simultaneously building a pipeline of larger, longer-term prospects.
Build and continuously manage a qualified pipeline of new prospects with clear revenue potential, strategy and next steps.
Personally open doors and create relationships with prospective donors and corporate partners, finding creative paths through personal relationships, community connections, events, research, professional networks and other channels.
Secure meetings and personally participate in cultivation, proposals, solicitations and closing opportunities.
Develop new corporate partnerships that can include sponsorships, program funding, employee engagement and longer-term organizational support.
Bring discipline and consistent follow-through to every promising opportunity.
Partner closely with the CEO on cultivation and solicitation strategy, including advising on important existing donor relationships when appropriate.
Maintain clear visibility into the prospect pipeline, activity, next steps, potential revenue and expected timing.

Existing Donor Relationships

Cancer Pathways has many long-standing donors with deep personal connections to the organization and its founder. Those relationships are incredibly important to us and require context, judgment and care.
The CEO will lead many of these relationships. This role will serve as a strategic fundraising partner — helping identify opportunities, develop individualized cultivation strategies, prepare for conversations, and determine when and how an ask makes sense. We believe relationships come before asks, particularly with people who have been part of Cancer Pathways for many years.
What We're Looking For

This is not a role for someone learning how to originate new relationships and revenue. Whether your background is in nonprofit development, corporate partnerships or relationship-based sales, you must have a demonstrated track record of personally developing new donor and/or corporate relationships that resulted in meaningful new revenue, and be able to speak to specific examples of how you created those opportunities and the results you personally produced.

How did you identify them, how did you get in the door, how did you develop the relationship, what you did to move the opportunity forward and ultimately what the result was.
Significant successful experience in major gifts, corporate development, nonprofit fundraising, strategic partnerships, relationship-based sales/business development or a closely related field. We are open to candidates from outside the nonprofit sector who can demonstrate exceptional success developing new relationships and generating revenue.
A demonstrated record of personally generating new donors, corporate relationships, clients, partnerships and/or new revenue - not simply managing or renewing an established donor portfolio.
Experience securing meaningful individual gifts, corporate commitments and/or sponsorships.
Exceptional relationship-building skills and strong interpersonal judgment.
The resourcefulness to identify prospects, find a path to them and create opportunities independently.
Strong knowledge of the Seattle/Puget Sound philanthropic and corporate community; existing relationships are highly valued.
The ability to balance urgency with thoughtful relationship development.
Confidence making meaningful asks when the relationship and opportunity are right.
Strong communication skills, judgment and follow-through.
A bias toward action, accountability and results.
The ability to operate independently and move quickly from strategy to execution.

We care far more about demonstrated fundraising results, relationships and judgment than degrees, titles or the size of the organizations you have worked for in the past. We’re interested in what you have PERSONALLY made happen.
How Success Will Be Measured

New philanthropic revenue secured
New individual donors and corporate partners acquired
Qualified new prospects and revenue opportunities created
Movement of prospects from identification through cultivation, solicitation and commitment
Strength and value of the forward revenue pipeline
Consistent execution, follow-through and measurable progress

Engagement & Compensation

This is a part-time independent contractor engagement of up to 20 hours per week. Some work can be performed remotely, but this is a Seattle-focused relationship role, and the contractor must be available for donor and prospect meetings, events and other important in-person opportunities throughout the greater Seattle area.
Compensation begins at $75/hour, with the opportunity for increased hourly compensation and/or fixed performance bonuses based on achievement of mutually agreed-upon fundraising, new-revenue and pipeline goals. Performance and compensation will be reviewed regularly.
The engagement is designed to provide flexibility for both Cancer Pathways and the contractor and may be ended by either party with appropriate notice.

How to Apply

Please send a resume along with a brief note describing your interest and relevant experience to info@cancerpathways.org.In your note, please include two or three examples of new donors or corporate relationships you personally developed (see “What We're Looking For” above for the specific points to address).

The Medical Affairs and Evidence Generation (MA&EG) Asset Lead provides expert medical insights to inform indication selection, target product profile development, clinical development plans, and pre-launch and commercialization strategies working with global cross-functional team members from science, clinical development, medical affairs and evidence generation, and commercial. This strategic leader serves in a “player coach” capacity with responsibilities for the Integrated Evidence Generation Plans and other relevant MA&EG activities working with the broader MA&EG community members who support the asset. FB-102 is a first-in-class anti-CD122 monoclonal antibody designed to selectively modulate pathogenic T-cell and NK-cell activity that drives autoimmune disease. About Palo Alto University (PAU)

Palo Alto University is a private, nonprofit university dedicated to advancing human understanding through innovative education, groundbreaking research, and impactful practice in behavioral science.
Founded in 1975 and located in the heart of Silicon Valley, PAU offers graduate and undergraduate programs in psychology, counseling, social work, and behavioral science, including the PAU-Stanford PsyD Consortium with Stanford Medicine. Grounded in human dignity, PAU’s scholars, clinicians, educators, and learners share a single conviction: that understanding how people think, feel, behave, relate, heal, and make meaning is among the most essential work of our time.
The university enrolls over 1,200 students, has a network of more than 4,200 alumni, and employs over 150 faculty and staff who are united by a mission-driven commitment to advancing human understanding. PAU enters its sixth decade at a defining moment: a new president, a new provost, a bold new vision and strategic plan, and an urgent opportunity to shape how behavioral science responds to the challenges of an increasingly changing world. You will join a mission-driven community with the ambition to make a measurable impact on the human condition.

About the Position

The Founding Executive Director of the Center for Translational Research in Behavioral Science will establish and lead a university-wide hub that expands PAU’s research capacity, advances faculty and student research development, increases external funding, fosters interdisciplinary and strategic partnerships, and accelerates the translation of behavioral science research into meaningful real-world impact.
The successful candidate will be an entrepreneurial and collaborative leader who can build the Center from the ground up while developing innovative approaches to strengthen PAU’s research culture, visibility, partnerships, and impact.

SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Center for Translational Research
Establish and lead the Center, including its strategy, programs, operations, budget, partnerships, and measures of success.
Supervise research-related functions including the library, IRB, grants, writing support, and research design and data analysis services.
Develop signature research initiatives that translate PAU scholarship into meaningful applications in practice, policy, technology, and communities.
Engage faculty across the University as Center affiliates, collaborators, and research leaders.
Build strategic partnerships with universities, healthcare organizations, community organizations, government, foundations, and industry.
Support Presidential initiatives and University advancement priorities by identifying and developing research opportunities, partnerships, and external engagement aligned with PAU’s strategic goals.

Research Innovation & Strategy
Actively build and expand PAU’s research enterprise and generate meaningful external revenue through grants, sponsored research, contracts, and strategic partnerships.
Establish and achieve measurable research growth and revenue targets aligned with PAU’s Strategic Plan, while ensuring that all activities advance the University’s academic mission, research priorities, and long-term sustainability.
Identify opportunities to strengthen research infrastructure, productivity, interdisciplinary collaboration, visibility, and impact.
Advance translational research aligned with PAU’s strengths in psychology, counseling, and social work.
Advance PAU’s signature research agenda at the intersection of human understanding and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, positioning the University as a distinctive and influential voice in one of the most consequential areas of inquiry and innovation of our time.
Oversee the full portfolio of technology transfer and commercialization activities, including technology and licensing agreements, intellectual property management, invention disclosures, technology partnerships, royalty arrangements, and equity interests.

Research Development & Support
Identify external funding opportunities and support faculty in developing competitive grant proposals.
Convene and support interdisciplinary teams pursuing collaborative and strategically important research opportunities.
Develop workshops, mentoring, seed funding, and other initiatives that strengthen faculty research capacity and student research competencies.
Collaborate with University offices responsible for finance, faculty success, advancement, and other areas supporting the research enterprise.

External Engagement & Impact
Represent PAU and the Center with research partners, funders, and professional organizations.
Develop opportunities for external research partnerships, sponsored research, and philanthropic support.
Increase the visibility of PAU research and communicate its scholarly and societal impact.
Leverage PAU’s Silicon Valley location to develop innovative partnerships at the intersection of behavioral science, mental health, technology, and human-centered innovation.
Develop and cultivate strategic relationships with startups, accelerators, and venture capital firms to build partnerships, advance commercialization opportunities, and generate sustainable long-term revenue streams.

ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS
PhD or equivalent terminal research doctorate in psychology, behavioral science, health science, social science, or another field related to PAU’s areas of expertise.
Minimum of 3–5 years of research administration, research development, sponsored research, or related experience in a university or research environment.
Progressive leadership experience with demonstrated success developing programs, initiatives, partnerships, or research infrastructure.
Demonstrated understanding of external research funding and the academic research enterprise.
Experience supporting competitive grant proposals and collaborative research initiatives.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively with students, faculty, academic leaders, and external partners.
Ability to work in person, with established professional networks and connections across the San Francisco Bay Area.
Excellent leadership, communication, organizational, and project-management skills.
Demonstrated ability to think strategically, build new initiatives, and work collaboratively across disciplines and organizational boundaries.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
Demonstrated success securing or contributing substantially to externally funded research.
Genuine interest in and intellectual curiosity about research at the intersection of human understanding, emerging technologies, and artificial intelligence.
Experience developing interdisciplinary, multi-investigator, or multi-institutional proposals.
Experience launching or leading a research center, institute, or major research initiative.
Experience with translational, applied, implementation, or community-engaged research.
Familiarity with federal funding agencies relevant to PAU, including NIH, NSF, HRSA, and SAMHSA.
Record of scholarly accomplishment and experience supporting faculty research development.
Experience developing partnerships across academia, healthcare, government, foundations, community organizations, or industry.

Are you a leader in nonprofit international development who has diversified an organization’s funding in order to expand its programs?

Would you welcome the chance to lead an innovative global nonprofit empowering women, girls and their families, and to scale the organization into its next phase of growth?

If this sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you!

PNP Staffing Group is excited to have been retained by Social Capital Initiatives to lead their search for an Executive Director.

JOB TITLE: Executive Director

SALARY: $150,000 - $160,000

LOCATION: Hybrid schedule in New York, NY

About Social Capital Initiatives

The mission of Social Capital Initiatives is to leverage the power of social capital to improve livelihoods in under-served communities by promoting education, healthcare, and sustainable development.

With a particular focus on women, girls, and their families, Social Capital Initiatives utilizes its proven Social Capital Credits (SoCCs) methodology—along with innovative programs and technologies—to empower people to realize their potential and become active stakeholders in their own success. Founded 26 years ago, Social Capital Initiatives now reaches more than 100,000 people every year across 25 communities in Asia, the U.S., Africa, and Europe.

Social Capital Initiatives now seeks to scale its projects and impact globally, particularly in the United States. To achieve this vision, Social Capital Initiatives is seeking a dynamic and visionary executive who can work with its Founder and the Board to scale the organization into its next stage of growth.

Position Overview

The ExecutiveDirector will drive the next chapter of Social Capital Initiatives’ growth and strategy, leading fundraising and partnerships. The Executive Director will be responsible for shaping and adapting the organization as it grows.

Key Responsibilities

Fundraising & Resource Development
: Drive transformational growth in fundraising by cultivating and diversifying major donors, corporate partnerships, foundations, and government funding sources. Set and deliver ambitious, board-approved fundraising goals.
Strategy & Vision
: Lead Social Capital Initiatives’ strategic refresh, setting transformational yet achievable goals with clear metrics for scaling its impact globally.
Partnerships & External Engagement
: Strengthen existing partnerships and establish new collaborations to expand the use of SoCCs, Cascades of Learning, and other Social Capital Initiatives programs, increasing visibility and learning across communities.
Board & Stakeholder Relations
: Develop and maintain constructive relationships with the Board of Directors, Board of Advisors, Junior Board, donors, partners, and community stakeholders.
Organizational Leadership
: Build, manage, and scale a global team aligned with Social Capital Initiatives mission and growth trajectory.
Operational & Financial Stewardship
: Partnering with the Founder, strengthen Social Capital Initiatives’ infrastructure, systems, and resources to support growth and long-term sustainability and success

Qualifications & Experience

Fundraising expertise, with established connections in the philanthropic community and demonstrated success with major donors, corporations, foundations, and government agencies. Knowledge of the corporate donor ecosystem in India is an added plus.
Deep demonstrated commitment to community-led development and empowerment, and the ability to represent the organization credibly with the communities it serves. Experience working with women and their families to help build social capital is highly valued.
Demonstrated leadership experience with progressive growth in nonprofit or for-profit organizations.
Proven track record scaling an organization, expanding programs, and strengthening operations to achieve greater impact.
Experience working effectively with a Board of Directors.
Strong financial and operational management skills.
Experience leading, empowering, and retaining diverse and global teams.
Public speaking excellence and the ability to inspire and persuade across small and large audiences.
Demonstrated commitment to international development and community empowerment; experience living or working in emerging markets is a plus.

Attributes & Competencies

Entrepreneurial approach to growth, sustainability, and innovation—balancing mission focus with business discipline.
Passion for Social Capital Initiatives’ mission, with deep commitment to community empowerment and sustainable development.
Strong cross-cultural competence, with the ability to collaborate effectively across diverse communities and geographies.
Versatile, hands-on, comfortable working with a small team.
Transparent, collaborative, and high-integrity leadership style.
Exceptional listening skills and ability to build trustamong staff, partners, and stakeholders.
Unwavering moral compass and the highest ethical standards.

Compensation

$150,000-160,000

Location / Work Arrangement

The Executive Director will be based in or travel frequently to the New York metropolitan area, with a flexible hybrid work arrangement, including in-person workdays and meetings. The role requires occasional domestic and international travel.

More about Social Capital Initiatives

Social Capital Initiatives is a New York-based 501(c)3 non-profit organization, founded in 1999 in Tokyo. It leverages the power of social capital to promote healthcare, education and sustainable development in underserved communities in India, the US, and other countries.

Our Social Capital Credits received the World Changing Idea Award from the Fast Company, as well as awards from MIT SOLVE, General Motors, Jacobs Foundation, and others. The organization enjoys the strong patronage of former Secretary-General of the United Nations, H.E. Ban Ki-moon, in whose honor the annual Ban Ki-moon Awards are bestowed. Awardees have included Mary Robinson, Nobel Laureate Joseph Stiglitz, Dr. Jane Goodall, and Gloria Steinem. Triple Grammy Award winning composer and environmentalist, Ricky Kej is our GoodwillAmbassador. Social Capital Initiatives has Special Consultative Status with the Economic and Social Council of the United Nations.

new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

The University of Utah (the U) seeks an accomplished, strategic, and collaborative leader to serve as its next executive director of housing operations within Housing & Dining Programs (HDP). Reporting to the associate vice president for Housing & Dining Programs and serving as a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the executive director will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of campus housing, informing enrollment and student success strategies, and providing strategic leadership for critical business and operational functions within a large, complex, and evolving university environment.

The executive director provides strategic leadership for a broad portfolio that includes Occupancy Management, Budget and Finance, Communications and Assessment, Technology and Housing Systems, and Living-Learning Programs. A central focus of the position will be developing and implementing strategies to strengthen demand for campus housing, optimize occupancy and revenue, enhance the residential student experience, and ensure that housing strategies align with the University's broader enrollment, academic, and student success priorities. The executive director will bring a data-informed, forward-thinking approach to these efforts, identifying opportunities to strengthen operations, improve effectiveness, and position HDP to respond successfully to evolving student needs and market conditions.

The executive director will join a highly collaborative leadership team committed to innovation, thoughtful decision-making, continuous improvement, and the long-term success of Housing & Dining Programs. The position offers the opportunity to work across institutional boundaries, build strong partnerships with key University stakeholders, and play an important role in advancing both the department's priorities and the University of Utah's broader strategic goals.

The executive director manages a dynamic team of 19 professionals, including four direct reports, and administers an annual budget of approximately $5 million.

Responsibilities

Occupancy, Enrollment, and Housing Strategy

Provide executive leadership for the U's housing occupancy strategy, including demand forecasting, application and contracting processes, room selection, assignments, and strategies designed to maximize utilization of the U's residential inventory.
Leverage enrollment, occupancy, market, and historical data to develop projections and identify opportunities to strengthen housing demand and achieve consistently high occupancy.
Partner closely with Enrollment Management, Admissions, academic colleges, Athletics, International Student Programs, and other institutional stakeholders to position housing as an important component of student recruitment, enrollment, retention, and success.

Business and Financial Leadership

Identify, research, and analyze strategic opportunities and evaluate their operational, fiscal, and policy implications in conjunction with centralized fiscal operations.
Provide recommendations to executive leadership that support sound decision-making and the long-term financial sustainability of Housing & Dining Programs.

Technology, Data, and Assessment

Maintain strategic oversight of housing technology and information systems, including the department's StarRez housing management platform, technology integrations, and systems supporting housing operations.
Champion a data-informed culture by ensuring that occupancy information, student feedback, assessment results, financial data, and institutional metrics translate into actionable strategies for continuous improvement.
Oversee the departmental assessment planning, data collection, analysis, reporting, and integration of findings into strategic and operational plans.

Communications, Marketing, and Outreach

Guide the strategic planning and implementation of departmental communications, marketing, outreach, and recruitment efforts.
Ensure that Housing & Dining Programs communicates effectively with prospective and current students, families, campus partners, and other stakeholders, and develops marketing and outreach strategies that support occupancy and enrollment objectives.

Living-Learning Programs

Set strategic priorities and provide executive oversight for the university's living-learning and themed residential communities.
Partner with academic colleges and other campus organizations to ensure residential programs support institutional priorities while creating meaningful opportunities for student engagement, belonging, and academic success.

Organizational Leadership

Recruit, develop, supervise, and evaluate professional staff while creating a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and professional growth.
Serve as a strategic advisor to the associate vice president and contribute broadly to the success of Housing & Dining Programs beyond the assigned portfolio.
Provide leadership through influence as well as positional authority, effectively navigating complex organizational environments and building productive relationships across the U.

University & Professional Engagement

Develop collaborative relationships and key partnerships across organizational and divisional boundaries, including, but not limited to, Enrollment Management, Admissions, Orientation & Transition, Athletics, International Student Support Services, academic colleges, Honors, Disability and Access, Commuter Services, General Counsel, University Guest House, University Marketing & Communications, and University Computing Services.
Represent Housing & Dining Programs on departmental, divisional, and university-wide committees.
Serve as an active connection to the broader collegiate housing profession through engagement with Big 12 institutions, the Association of College and University Housing Officers-International (ACUHO-I), and other relevant professional networks, while supporting team members in developing and strengthening their own professional connections.
Participate in departmental emergency and crisis response and, as appropriate, serve within the escalation and reporting structure for significant incidents occurring outside normal business hours.

Minimum Qualifications

The successful candidate will possess a bachelor's degree in business administration or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience. A master's degree in higher education, student affairs, business administration, or a related field is preferred. Candidates should also bring at least eight years of progressively responsible professional experience, including significant management and leadership responsibilities within university housing, student affairs, enrollment management, auxiliary services, or a comparably complex organization to the role. Other requirements include demonstrated success in supervising, developing, and leading professional staff; managing budgets and complex initiatives; and guiding organizational change. Additionally, the executive director must possess strong analytical and project-management capabilities, including the ability to use data to inform strategy and decision-making, as well as excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.

Competitive Candidates Will Demonstrate Several Of The Following Qualifications

A sophisticated understanding of the interrelationship among housing, enrollment management, student recruitment and retention, and broader institutional strategy.
Proven ability to develop housing demand and occupancy projections using enrollment trends, historical performance, market conditions, and operational data.
A record of developing and executing strategies that achieve and sustain housing occupancy of 95 percent or greater in highly competitive markets.
Expertise in managing occupancy throughout the full recruitment and assignment cycle, including early-, mid-, and late-cycle strategies.
Familiarity with housing management platforms; knowledge of StarRez is particularly desirable.
Leadership of housing application, contracting, assignment, and occupancy-management processes.
The ability to synthesize data, assessment findings, stakeholder feedback, and industry practices into actionable strategies and meaningful organizational change.
Skill in navigating, negotiating, and resolving complex or sensitive matters involving students, families, campus stakeholders, and institutional partners.
Knowledge of federal and state laws, regulations, and compliance requirements affecting university housing, including privacy, disability accommodations, emotional support animals, and landlord-tenant considerations.

Preferences

In addition to the qualifications stated above, key stakeholders identified the following capabilities and attributes of a successful candidate:

Extensive collaboration skills at all levels, with the ability to understand the vital importance of interconnectedness and solid relationships, while also serving as a strategic and visionary risk-taker who promotes creativity in every area of the position.
A compassionate, empathetic leader with the proven ability to make difficult decisions, quickly resolve issues before they escalate to become problems, conduct difficult conversations when pertinent, work effectively with staff members at various levels of development and knowledge, listen actively to all sides of an issue, and be willing to change directions as necessary.
The ability to navigate complex stakeholder environments and juggle multiple priorities, while maintaining a strategic vision of how all the various pieces fit together effectively.
Strong organizational development abilities, including emotional intelligence, transparency, excellent listening skills, an orientation to detail, and empathy that inspire and unify staff, provide professional and personal growth opportunities, and promote teamwork throughout the operation.
An innovator with a futuristic orientation and a willingness to try new opportunities, remain informed on recent trends and best practices, and drive significant change processes.

The Role We are hiring an Executive Director to run the business side of the firm. This is the most senior position in the firm after the equity partners, with responsibility for the entire back office: people and HR, day-to-day administration, finance and billing workflows, technology, and the teams that run them. You will work directly with firm owners, and you will execute through your team leads in finance, IT, and HR.
Our equity partners are excited about change. They have made the decision to grow, and they are looking for an operator they can empower to drive Sheppard the firm through that growth. You will have real authority to set priorities, make staffing and process decisions, and be accountable for results. If you have run operations for a law firm or professional services firm and want to lead rather than administer, this is that job.

What You'll Do •     Lead the firm back office: with all lines of reporting ultimately leading to you.
•     Partner through our managed services vendor to leverage centralized resources that drive growth.
•     Manage full-cycle recruiting and onboarding for paralegals, legal assistants, and staff, including managing outside recruiters, and partner with our managed services on attorney hiring so headcount keeps pace with client growth.
•     Own accountability across the back office. Set and reinforce operating standards for all back-office employees, create clarity of performance expectations, and win new business.
•     Direct daily business operations: office administration, facilities, business registrations, firm insurance, and records.
•     Own the annual operating budget with the Managing Partners; monitor efficiency ratios and prepare management discussion and analysis.
•     Drive the billing cycle through the finance lead — timely time entry, pre-bill review, carrier billing-guideline compliance, regular rate increase requests, WIP follow-up, and collections.
•     Lead firmwide HR: performance management, compensation and benefits, engagement, employee relations, payroll, and compliant employment practices.
•     Manage IT workflows with the firm's IT manager and managed services provider, and drive adoption and continuous education of practice management, AI-assisted timekeeping, and e-billing tools across the firm.
•     Translate firm strategy into a clear one-page plan and quarterly OKRs, and hold the firm accountable to them.

How Success Is Measured You will have clear targets and the authority to hit them. The headline measure is growth in the firm's bottom line of 15% or more per year; supporting it are staffing ratios across the back office, firm eNPS, timely time entry and pre-bill review by all timekeepers, paralegal and attorney success, billing cycle time, realization and write-down rates, and audit readiness. Our business partner provides the dashboards and reporting — you will not be building measurement systems from scratch. Your job is to run the firm off the numbers and move them.

Compensation •     $140,000 base salary.
•     30% target annual bonus, based on the firm's bottom-line growth (15%+ per year) and the related operating KPIs above.
•     $10,000 signing bonus.
•     Full benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), and paid time off.

What You Bring •     8+ years of operations HR leadership, including 3+ years running the business side of a law firm or professional services firm of 20+ people.
•     Strong leadership ability and energy, with hands-on experience in HR, payroll, recruiting, and employee relations.
•     A track record of owning a budget and growing the bottom line through staffing and process decisions.
•     Working knowledge of law-firm billing and collections, including timekeeping standards, pre-bill review, and client billing guidelines; insurance defense and e-billing experience strongly preferred.
•     Strong technology fluency and comfort leading change; experience with Clio and AI-assisted timekeeping tools is a plus.
•     Sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to have direct conversations with attorneys and staff.
•     Bachelor's degree.

Why Righi Fitch •     The most senior back-office seat in the firm, you are empowered to drive growth and change.
•     Strong business resources made available by our central services provider.
•     A rapidly growing firm with a clear path from 50+ to 100+ people, and the mandate to build the operating platform that gets it there.
•     Institutional-grade finance, reporting, technology, and recruiting support from Catalex, so you can focus on people, execution, and results.

The Director of Development leads IA&A's philanthropic strategy and is responsible for building the organization's contributed revenue base across foundations, government sources, corporate partners, and individual donors. IA&A has historically operated on a near-total reliance on earned revenue. The 2026-2030 strategic plan calls for a more diversified model in which contributed revenue becomes a meaningful and growing share of the organization's resource base. The Director of Development is the architect of that shift.

The work includes building IA&A's first sustained culture of philanthropy, developing a major gifts program, deepening foundation and government grant work, growing corporate partnerships tied to the organization's cultural diplomacy mission, and supporting the Board's expanded role in fundraising. The Director works in close partnership with the President & CEO, who personally cultivates and closes major funders, and collaborates with the COO, Vice President of Exhibitions and other senior staff to develop fundable programs and a compelling case for support.

Duties and responsibilities

Strategy & Planning

Develop and execute a multi-year contributed revenue plan aligned with the 2026-2030 strategic plan, with annual goals across foundation, government, corporate, individual, and planned giving sources.
Build IA&A's first sustained culture of philanthropy across staff, Board, and external supporters in an organization that has not historically relied on contributed income.
Partner with the CEO and senior program leadership to identify fundable programs and shape compelling cases for support, including for the integration of TES, Hillyer, and CEP as a unified cultural diplomacy platform.
Establish the policies, systems, and reporting needed to support a growing development operation, including within the Bloomerang and Monday CRM systems, gift acceptance, recognition, and donor stewardship practices.

Foundation & Government Funding

Cultivate and steward a portfolio of institutional funders, including private and family foundations, DCAH, the National Endowment for the Arts, the National Endowment for the Humanities, and other government cultural programs.
Oversee all grant writing and reporting, including direct authorship of major proposals and supervision of any external grant writers or consultants.
Build a balanced pipeline of project-restricted and general operating support.

Corporate & International Partnerships

Develop a corporate giving and sponsorship program connected to IA&A's cultural diplomacy mission, with particular attention to companies with international footprints and brands aligned with arts and culture.
Build sponsorship opportunities tied to specific exhibitions, programs, and events, including exhibition tours, Hillyer programming, and signature convenings.
In partnership with the CEO, identify and develop funding relationships with embassies, international foundations, and binational cultural organizations.

Individual Giving & Major Gifts

Build IA&A's individual donor base, including a focused major gifts program calibrated to the organization's size and growth stage.
Personally manage a portfolio of major donor prospects; staff the CEO and Board members on their portfolios with briefings, materials, and follow-through.
Develop annual giving, membership, and donor engagement structures sized to what is sustainable for an organization of IA&A's scale, and build a planned giving program over time.

Board Engagement

Support 100% Board giving and active Board engagement in fundraising; work with the CEO and Board leadership to formalize give/get expectations.
Staff the Development Committee (or any merged Development and Nominating committee structure) and serve as the senior staff resource for Board fundraising activity.
Equip Board members with the tools, briefings, and prospect support they need to participate appropriately in cultivation and solicitation.

Events, Communications & Donor Experience

Plan and execute fundraising and cultivation events, including donor receptions, exhibition openings, and signature annual events.
Use Hillyer and the IA&A programmatic calendar as a primary platform for donor cultivation and stewardship.
Work with the Communications staff to ensure development materials, donor communications, and the public case for support are consistent with the IA&A brand and strategic plan.

Team & Operations

Build and lead the development function, including any Development staff and management of external development consultants.
Maintain accurate donor records, gift processing, and reporting; provide regular forecasting to the CEO and Board.
Recruit and onboard additional development staff as the function grows and capacity is justified.
Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Seven or more years of progressive fundraising experience in the nonprofit sector; experience in arts, culture, museums, or international affairs preferred.
Demonstrated success building or substantially growing a development program, including direct authorship of grants and direct cultivation of major gifts.
